newsitem.title: USA: Focus on CBOT March corn before expiration.
newsitem.headline: Focus on CBOT March corn before expiration.

text.p: CBOT March grain and soy complex contracts were slated to expire Wednesday at 1201 CST/1800 GMT and traders said the focus was on March corn because of the relatively high open interest in that contract.
"There's 24 million (bushels) in the March corn open and there should be around 10 million (open)," a trader said.

CBOT preliminary figures Tuesday showed the open interest in the March contract at 24.0 million bushels. But that tally was down sharply from roughly 43 million bushels open in that contract at the start of trading Monday which led to diminished concerns about a volatile expiration in the March.
Market action as of 1100 CST Tuesday also indicated position holders in the March were continuing a quick but "rational" exit.
Continental Grain had bear spread 400,000 bushels of July/March and spread three million July/May while Tenco Inc bear spread 2.5 million bushels of the May/March, traders said.
Traders said up until early dealings Tuesday, there had been some concern the key commercial firm would remain stuck in the March corn contract going into the expiration bell.
"Tenco stopped the corn (Tuesday deliveries) and bull spread 2-1/2 million May/March so that is taking a lot of pressure off the March," a trader said.
The CBOT early Monday increased to $1,755 the margin in the March corn contract from the previous $810.
Open interest totals in the other March contracts were at "comfortable levels," traders said.

The CBOT early Tuesday said the preliminary open interest in March soybeans was at 5.3 million bushels, soymeal at 1,671 lots and soyoil at 1,617 lots, March wheat at 860,000 bushels and oats at 640,000 bushels.
